result.title: Quantization for Action, Execution for Deployment: Joint Precision and Execution Selection for World Action Models
result.summary: World action models guide robots by predicting the effects of actions or generating commands from observations. A model may compare hundreds of candidate futures before acting, repeatedly reading weights that must fit in device memory. Post-training quantization reduces the number of bits used to store pretrained weights, but a smaller model is not necessarily a deployable one: temporary tensors can exceed graphics processing unit (GPU) memory limits, while even small prediction errors can change the selected action. This creates two coupled challenges: identifying bit assignments that preserve task performance and determining which of them meet real execution constraints, without exhausting costly task trials. We present PTQ4WAM, a framework for choosing layer-wise bit assignments and execution routes under memory, latency and task-evaluation budgets. Calibration measurements guide candidate proposals, optionally with a language model agent. We profile full-model routes on the GPU before spending task trials on feasible assignments. Fusing group rescaling and reading visual history in place can make an otherwise infeasible assignment deployable. Across 15 workloads from four model families, the median task score is 99.2% of the corresponding 32-bit floating-point (FP32) score. On fixed GPU replays, the median speedup over FP32 is 2.36 times and the median reduction in peak allocated memory is 71.5%. The code will be released soon.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PTQ4WAM，在显存、延迟与任务评测预算约束下为 world action models 选择分层量化位宽与执行路线，用校准测量与 GPU profiling 先筛掉不可行方案，再投入昂贵的任务试验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按校准灵敏度分配精度、以廉价测量替代昂贵任务验证的预算化筛选思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中「哪些内部状态或计算值得保留」及动态计算成本权衡的评价方式，但属较远领域线索。
